title: Finite coefficient multiplication respects the specified pullback compositor
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite extension E of Q_l, with the finite quotient coefficient sheaf B_{T,m} of exponent m+1 on each scheme T [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-constant-coefficient-objects]. For composable scheme maps f:X→Y and g:Y→Z and m≥0, let d_f be the regular finite pullback unit multiplication [lem-zl-coefficient-pullback-unit-coordinates], and c_{f,g} the specified finite compositor [def-zl-finite-regular-coefficient-comparisons]. Then c_{f,g}(B_{Z,m}) followed by Lf*(d_g) and d_f equals d_{f≫g}.

source.place: Constant-sheaf clause; reviewed expansion of lem-zl-constant-geometric-stalk-unit, step 3

proof.text: Transpose multiplication along the module adjunctions. Its transpose is the regular section one. The coefficient direct-image maps respect composition, so the direct-image compositor carries the two successive section-one maps to the section-one map for the composite. The existing finiteIntrinsicPullback_unit_comp theorem supplies precisely the adjunction-generator formula for the intrinsic ordinary compositor; the ordinary characterization of the canonical derived ringed-site compositor supplies its other presentation.

proof.text: The specified changes of pullback coordinates preserve the adjunction units. Consequently uniqueness of transposes identifies the canonical ordinary pullback compositor with the multiplication-preserving map. Equivalently, on pure tensors both paths multiply the same coefficients. The tensor balancing relation and sheafification make this equality hold on all sections.

proof.text: The regular module in degree zero is a flat-term K-flat representative. Exact localization and naturality of the single-complex comparisons preserve the ordinary equality, giving the displayed derived equation. Identity maps, empty schemes and the exponent-one quotient require no extra hypothesis.

theorem finiteUnit_composition
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (m : ℕ) :
    (finiteCanonicalPullbackComposition l E f g m).hom.app
        (finiteConstantCoefficientObject l E Z m) ≫
      (finiteDerivedPullback l E m f).map (finiteUnit l E g m).hom ≫
        (finiteUnit l E f m).hom = (finiteUnit l E (f ≫ g) m).hom
